scenes.text: Fine-tuning a huge AI model used to need a room full of expensive GPUs. [1] Today, you can do it on a single gaming graphics card. [2] The trick is called LoRA. Let's see how it works.

title: LoRA
Explained
data.subtitle: Fine-tuning on a budget
data.hook: Train your own AI on *one GPU*

scenes.text: First, a quick reminder from episode 18. [1] Full fine-tuning updates every single weight in the model, billions of numbers. It's slow, and needs huge memory. [2] LoRA freezes the original model, and trains a tiny add-on instead. Often less than one percent of the size.

[1] LoRA stands for low rank adaptation. [2] Think of the big model as a thick textbook. [3] Instead of rewriting the whole book, you stick a few sticky notes inside, [4] and the notes change how the book is read.

data.definition: Low-Rank Adaptation: keep the big model frozen and train small add-on matrices that adjust its behaviour.

scenes.text: Here's how it works. [1] Take a pretrained model and freeze all its weights. [2] Attach small adapter matrices to some of its layers. [3] Train only those adapters on your own examples. [4] Save the adapter, often just a few megabytes. [5] At run time, plug it in, and the model behaves in your custom way.

So where is LoRA used? [1] Image generators learn a new art style, or a person's face, from a few photos. [2] Companies teach a chatbot their tone and product terms. [3] And one base model can swap between many adapters, like a lawyer mode, and a doctor mode.

data.heading: Where it's used
items: A new art style from a few pictures

scenes.text: Here are four terms. [1] Adapter, the small trainable add-on. [2] Rank, how big the adapter is. Smaller rank means fewer numbers. [3] Frozen weights, the original model that stays unchanged. [4] And QLoRA, LoRA on a compressed model, so it fits on even smaller GPUs.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think LoRA is a weaker, low quality shortcut. [2] For many tasks, it gets close to full fine-tuning results, at a fraction of the cost. But it can't add huge amounts of new knowledge. For fresh facts, use RAG.

data.myth: LoRA is a weak, low quality shortcut.
data.fact: For many tasks it gets close to full fine-tuning at a fraction of the cost. For fresh facts, use RAG.
data.tip: LoRA for style and skills, RAG for facts

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] LoRA freezes the big model. [2] It trains tiny adapters instead. [3] Adapters are just a few megabytes, and swappable. [4] It's great for style and skills, while RAG handles facts. [5] Next, RAG part two, chunking and vector databases. Follow AI Maastaaru!
